items.stem: Claude drafts a revenue formula that returns a plausible total. Before using it in the model, what is the essential step?

options.text: Trace the formula's inputs and reconcile the output to the source data
options.rationale: Correct: plausible totals can still be wrong; tracing and reconciling is essential.

options.text: Accept it because the number looks reasonable
options.rationale: A reasonable-looking number is not a verified one.

options.text: Lock the cell so no one can review it
options.rationale: Hiding the formula prevents the review it needs.

items.explanation: Correct: plausible totals can still be wrong; tracing and reconciling is essential.

items.stem: Which TWO practices make a Claude-assisted financial model easier to review? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Keeping assumptions on a separate, sourced inputs sheet
options.rationale: Correct: explicit assumptions support transparent review.

options.text: Building independent checks that flag broken links
options.rationale: Correct: sanity checks catch errors before they mislead.
Hidden constants are hard to review and audit.

options.text: Removing all labels to save space
options.rationale: Unlabelled models are harder, not easier, to review.

items.explanation: Correct: explicit assumptions support transparent review.

items.stem: How should model outputs be described to a decision-maker?

options.text: As conditional estimates that depend on stated assumptions
options.rationale: Correct: outputs are only as good as their assumptions and should be framed that way.

options.text: As precise facts that cannot change
options.rationale: Model outputs are conditional, not fixed facts.
The model reflects the author's assumptions, not an independent opinion.
